main_body: Thatched hut: a large thatch roof slope (rows 5-54) over a log-plank front wall with a central framed door and two round shields (rows 55-78)
top_band: Thatch roof slope from row 6 to about row 54: golden bands (L 124 with L 154 highlights and L 69 shadow lines), under a dark ridge outline at rows 5-6
evidence: The roof reads as a big lighter sloped top surface, like the Beodeul house references. The darker log wall sits clearly below it, so the roof-to-wall step is a strong tone change. The eave line at about row 54 has a dark shadow row under it. The door is inset, with a wooden frame, a dark interior and a stone threshold. No isometric side faces are drawn. This matches how the reference buildings are built.

style.evidence: The outline is tinted dark brown (only 13% of dark edge pixels are neutral), so it does not look like a sticker. The thatch roof is the main weakness. It is a huge area built from about 4 tones in perfectly regular horizontal stripes with a repeated tick pattern, so it looks mechanical and flatter than the shaded roof tiles of the references. There is no clump variation and no per-tile or per-bundle highlights. The log wall has better variation. Distinct colours (38) are far below both references (66 and 185), and median colours per tile (9) is below both (11 and 18). That supports slightly lower density and shallower shading, so it would look thinner next to the references.
